Reseña de RUINER

RUINER es un shooter cyberpunk brutal, rápido y extremadamente estilizado que logra destacar gracias a su atmósfera opresiva y su combate frenético. Aunque no es un juego muy largo, consigue dejar una fuerte impresión por su personalidad visual y ritmo intenso.

La historia ocurre en una ciudad futurista dominada por corporaciones y tecnología violenta. El protagonista, un personaje silencioso con un casco lleno de símbolos digitales, debe rescatar a su hermano mientras enfrenta hordas de enemigos y descubre conspiraciones dentro del sistema.

Uno de los mayores puntos fuertes es el combate. RUINER mezcla disparos, ataques cuerpo a cuerpo y habilidades especiales en enfrentamientos extremadamente rápidos donde morir puede ocurrir en segundos.

El gameplay constantemente obliga al jugador a moverse, esquivar ataques y usar habilidades estratégicamente. Quedarse quieto normalmente significa morir muy rápido.

Visualmente el juego es espectacular. Su estética cyberpunk llena de neones, lluvia, pantallas gigantes y violencia tecnológica crea una ambientación increíblemente intensa y memorable.

La música electrónica también es excelente y acompaña perfectamente la velocidad y brutalidad del combate.

El sistema de habilidades agrega bastante variedad, permitiendo adaptar el estilo de juego usando mejoras enfocadas en hackeo, fuerza, velocidad o armas específicas.

La atmósfera del mundo también ayuda muchísimo. Aunque la historia es relativamente simple, el diseño visual y ambiental logra transmitir sensación constante de decadencia y control corporativo.

Sin embargo, RUINER puede ser bastante difícil y agresivo para algunos jugadores. Los combates muchas veces exigen reflejos rápidos y bastante precisión.

Además, la narrativa no siempre explica demasiado bien ciertos elementos del mundo o personajes, dejando varias cosas algo confusas.

La duración también es relativamente corta comparada con otros juegos de acción modernos.

Aun así, RUINER sigue siendo una experiencia cyberpunk increíblemente intensa y uno de los shooters indie más estilizados y frenéticos de los últimos años.

Calificación: 8.5/10

I liked Ruiner. I liked it so much that I will definitely check out the second game, and I urge everyone that is open minded to try this game. It's a short and sweet game that does a lot of right things.

Heads up, this is all from a perspective of playing it on normal. So I won't be able to talk about what harder difficulties do, or what NG+ does. I heard it doesn't change the story and only ups the difficulty, but does carry over your progress so I might try it down the line.

First of all, do not listen to anyone that says this is similar to Hotline Miami. It's different and you will feel it if you have played Hotline Miami before. The thing is, with Hotline Miami, you know the layout of the map with every enemy placement and what weapon they have. You plan around what enemies have and what you have and every mistake you make is punished with death everytime (unless you got the 2 tap mask). 

Ruiner isn't like this. It's a reaction based game that has you making decisions on the fly as enemies drop into the level after you enter specific combat spots. And you aren't killed in one shot, and so aren't your enemies. So don't buy it with the expectation of playing Hotline Miami. 

I still do recommend it. The combat is engaging and fun, with abilites that you can swap anytime you want. Which is fun, as you can change up what strategy to use in each boss. 

I think the main bosses are kind of a bummer though. I really liked the mini-bosses. They genuinely are hard and you frequently use your abilities and do have to play into their weaknesses. 

But with the bosses, most of the time it feels like I'm playing DMC2. If you played DMC2, you might have just groaned. Just hold down the trigger until the boss dies. It's so rough cause there isn't a way to get close and try hacking away at the boss as you get punished everytime you do without a doubt. I heard that in NG+ that enemies enter the boss arena and attack along side the boss, but I don't know how that feels.

Other than that, there is an arena mode which I didn't go into it a lot, but tried it a bit. It's a mode where you fight waves of enemies while getting upgrades every wave. It's challenging enough and I think it's fun enough to sink your teeth into. 

Other than the gameplay, the environment is gorgeous with this massive emphasis on red. And I mean MASSIVE, to the point that it might be drowning. But the cyberpunk esthetic is processed beautifully in a weird way. It carries style with everything you see, which is also reflected in the character designs that ooze style. Even the enemies have this nice and satisfying design. But again, every level is coated in red with no change whatsoever. So that might bore some people.

There is a little hub area where you can converse with people, explore, and do some stuff. I thought it was neat and fun enough. It keeps it fresh between missions and builds a bit of context that I appreciate.

The soundtrack is pretty good, nothing home to write about. I did enjoy it though, it helped the experience a lot. The cutscenes were pretty cool too, sometimes they were 3D rendered and sometimes they were animated. I thought it was nice. But one of the biggest gripes, it needs voice acting. I wish they commited to it, cause there are people that say a line or 2. It kinda makes the game feel silent at time since no one speaks. 

Now, story. Minor spoilers for people who care.

I personally didn't mind it. The plot twist was pretty good tbh, I thought it was a nice and neat way to pack up what had transpired. They were a little on the nose with how Her kept calling us "puppy", so I wouldn't be surprised if everyone caught on with the fact that she is using us for a reason. But other than that plot twist, the reasoning they give for everything that happened in the game was pretty nice and made a lot of sense. It placed everything in a nice knot and set it up nicely for a sequel which I'm kinda excited for. 

All in all, Ruiner is a fun game that knew how much runtime it needed and packed a lot of nice things into the runtime it had. I hope the sequel isn't going to be a bloated mess and I hope they stray away from the red, please. It's starting to hurt my eyes.

It's a beautiful game and pretty solid for what it is. But I'm learning that these kind of games aren't for me anymore. I don't know why, they just don't grab me like they used to. I do recommend it tho for those who love top down, run & gun shooters.

What I liked in this game? Music (the best part), smooth gameplay, Miami Hotline style, cyberpunk aesthetics, color palate (surprisingly, even though almost everything is red), South Korean and Chinese language. What I didn't like? The world could have been developed better - the city, characters, exploration. Levels are repetitive.

In this future people are used as tools and we are no exception. Who we are? What do we want? The voice in our head says we need to do something, then one mean voice switches to another. But from outside perspective - nothing changed. So the Ruiner, like the player, clings to the idea of purpose - to do what he does, to do what he only knows. The vague reason is enough to kill hundreds. Its all red around us, glowing, shining, blinking, so blood will not be that visible. Or we see everything in red tones because of the damn helmet and its used as a filter to change our perspective? Who knows. We just move and ruin everything on our way in a righteous crusade, painting everything red. And after the dust settles, when I finally come to the truth - I felt alone, betrayed and empty. I felt used. But I WAS used from the very start anyway...Guess I need more red cover to stop thinking about it. The voice says - "go puppy xD". And I think I am going.

From the gameplay perspective - its a high octane top-down action shooter (while you can spec in melee), where you fight with multiple enemies, both melee and range, regular and bosses in small arenas in a very fast pace (it even has a dedicated speedrun mode to cut out the plot), where you char also has multiple abilities (you can set up up to 5, from a dozen), and it appreciates flexibility, since you need to adapt to situation fast, so you can respec anytime you want, even multiple times in the same fight. The main character is not dying from 1 hit, but he is rather fragile (so are the enemies, even bosses, where boss fights can last seconds/less than a minute).
It is very stylish, dark, gory, bloody and it has a great witchhouse soundtrack including Zamilska, Sidewalks and Skeletons (sleep paralysis, memory, drifter, the end songs among the others), and one of my favorites "Island Door" (Paranesian Circle) by Susumu Hirasawa.
It is kinda hard, but its a very short fast pased game, that you must try if you like cyberpunk and good music. One of the best games I ever played.

It's just so damn cool. The story is hand-wavy and the gameplay kinda gets samey (it has enough highs tho, tbf), but damn are the visuals and music so cool. I loved the soundtrack and the character arts, the atmosphere is so immersive. The game does such a great job not overstaying its welcome, and that may be its biggest strength, honestly.

Be ready to let your imagination do some of the work, it's gonna be a great time if you do.

Это первая моя игра такого типа. Затянуло не по детски и прошел игру на одном дыхании за одну игровую сессию. 
Решил сыграть на харде (ведь это совет разработчиков) и уже на первом уровне понял - это будет боль. 
Сам по себе игровой процесс - это арена шутер видом сверху и короткими перебежками между аренами. Оружие достаточно разнообразное (как ближебойное, так и стрелковое). Враги также отличаются (но не слишком сильно, ядро у них все-таки одно). Порадовала прокачка способностей: она не статична и есть возможность изменить способности в любой момент времени и попробовать что-нибудь новое. Все быстро, шустро, динамично. 
Визуально игра выглядит красиво. Этакий около-киберпанк, только мрачный. 
Сюжет - 5/10. Тут во главе угла все-таки геймплей, поэтому некритично. Никакого "вау эффекта" я не испытал от него.
Музыка - тут я разочаровался. Мне запомнилась только одна композиция из всего того, что играло на протяжении всей игры.

По итого, строго советую данную игру. Если вы любите сложности и подобного типа игры, тогда эта игра точно для вас

Este es de esos juegos que desde el minuto uno te tiran a pelear sin descanso, y si te quedas quieto, estás muerto.

Lo mejor sin duda es la ambientación. Todo ese rollo cyberpunk con neones, suciedad, tecnología y violencia está muy bien logrado. La música electrónica acompaña perfecto y hace que todo se sienta más intenso.

El combate es rápido, agresivo y bastante exigente. No es solo disparar sin pensar, tienes que moverte, usar habilidades y adaptarte. Me gustó mucho poder cambiar las habilidades en cualquier momento, eso le da variedad.

Eso sí, no todo es perfecto. Los escenarios pueden sentirse repetitivos y la historia está ahí, pero no es lo más importante ni lo mejor contado. Además, la dificultad a veces se pasa y puede frustrar.

Aun así, es una experiencia corta pero muy intensa, ideal si te gustan los juegos de acción directa.
